big_idea: We can model ANY community situation. Pick a topic, ask a question, build a model.
learning_intention: We are learning to model a real-life community situation from our own life.
student_learning_goal: I can model a real-life community situation from my own life.
success_criteria: I can pick a community situation that interests me.
I can walk through the modelling cycle.
I can share my model with the class.
lesson_specific_materials: Coach Cara and Sport Sam together
Lesson 5 capstone tracker — provided in assessment_suite stage

minds_on.hook: Now you model YOUR community. Pick a situation. Walk through all 5 steps.
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Coach Cara + Sport Sam together. 'Friends — today you become MATHEMATICAL MODELLERS. Pick a community situation. Walk through the cycle: SITUATION, QUESTION, DATA, PREDICT, REFLECT.'

Show modelling cycle chart. 'You've practiced each step. Today you do them ALL together at COMMUNITY scale.'

Show examples:
- 'Hockey rink: how many goals scored in a season? Data → predict → reflect.'
- 'Library: how many books returned per month? Big numbers, big predictions.'
- 'Restaurant: how many pizzas per Saturday? Predict for a year.'
- 'School bus: how many trips per term? Data over weeks.'
- 'Park: how many dog walkers? Trends across seasons.'

'Coach Cara says — pick something from YOUR community. Walk through the 5 steps. Use big numbers. We share at the end.'

steps.instruction: Hand out capstone templates. Children pick a community topic and walk through the modelling cycle.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say: 'Use the template. Walk through ALL 5 steps. Big-scale numbers.'

steps.instruction: Children work for 12-15 minutes individually. Teacher circulates.
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each child. Check completeness.

steps.instruction: Stretch challenge: include a refinement based on data.
Gallery walk: children swap and read each other's models.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say: 'Swap. Read. Tell them ONE thing you liked.'
Pick variety: rink, library, restaurant, bus, park.

differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide picture-supported templates with sentence frames.
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Allow them to act out their model with classmates.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: picks coherent topic; walks through all 5 steps; shares with class.
formative_check.how_to_record: Tick the capstone tracker per child.

consolidation.activity_name: Coach Cara's Closing Brag and Certificate Ceremony
discussion_prompts: What's the most surprising community model you saw today?
Why do we use the modelling CYCLE?
What community situation will you model after this unit?
What's the difference between data and prediction?
consolidation.exit_routine: Each child receives a Junior Community Modeller certificate. Whisper: 'My model was about ___'.

assessment_in_this_lesson.evidence_collected: Full modelling cycle from a child-chosen community topic.
assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 5 captures C4 summative integration at community scale.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child picks a too-small topic for community scale — repairing the wrong-scale trap at Grade 3 capstone
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
The most common Grade-3 trap on the capstone is the wrong-scale trap: child picks a single-day, single-classroom topic instead of a community-scale one. The model lacks the multiplication-by-time depth.

This matters because Grade-3 modelling expects scaling.

The walkthrough covers when child picks 'how many lunches in my class today'.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Child writes 'how many lunches in my class today: 24'. Teacher reads.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Great topic, but small scale. Coach Cara wants COMMUNITY scale. Try: how many lunches in MY SCHOOL all week? 24 kids x 5 days = 120. Or in my COMMUNITY all month? Bigger numbers.'

The child rewrites. Generalise. 'Coach Cara says — community scale means hundreds or thousands. Multiply your local count by time and population.'

If still too small: provide scaling prompts. 'My class x 5 days = ___. My school x 1 month = ___. My community x 1 season = ___.' Force the scaling.

Long-term recovery: every capstone uses community-scale numbers.
expected_student_responses: (Strong) Picks community-scale topic with multi-time-span data.
common_misconceptions: Small topics are easier. (Repair: scaling demonstrates Grade-3 depth.)
Big numbers are scary. (Repair: multiplication handles scale.)
I can't think of community examples. (Repair: rink, library, restaurant, park.)

parts_outline.task: Reflection — would my model need refining?
